events.event_title: US-China Tariff Escalation & Trade War Reignition
events.event_description: The Trump administration has imposed sweeping tariffs on Chinese imports (up to 145%), with China retaliating at 125%. This is disrupting supply chains, forcing reshoring decisions, and creating acute margin pressure for importers while benefiting domestic manufacturers. A near-term catalyst is any negotiation announcement or further escalation in the coming weeks.
events.rationale: DXPE and POWL are domestic industrial equipment makers benefiting from reshoring capex. KTOS benefits from defense/domestic manufacturing tailwinds. ARCB (trucking) sees mixed signals — volume disruption but potential rate recovery as import patterns shift. GFF (Griffon Corp) makes US-manufactured building products and gains pricing power as Chinese competitors face tariffs.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $160 on tariff escalation news or break below $152 on tariff negotiation rumors; RSI confirmation above 50 signals momentum
tickers.exit_condition: Trade tariff deal announcement, RSI >70 (overbought exit), or close below $150 (thesis break)
tickers.risk: Rapid tariff reversal/negotiation surprise, DXPE margin compression if input costs rise faster than pricing power, demand destruction in industrial capex if recession fears spike

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $215 on tariff escalation news or China retaliation announcement; alternatively, dip to $200-203 RSI <35 on any negotiation optimism fade
tickers.exit_condition: US-China trade deal announcement or tariff rollback; RSI >70; failure to hold $210 on next tariff headline; time stop at 8 weeks if no material move
tickers.risk: Tariff negotiation breakthrough (Trump/China deal removes thesis); POWL supply chain already partially hedged/diversified (less reshoring benefit than peers); margin compression if input costs rise faster than pricing power materializes; RSI at 39 suggests limited downside cushion before technical breakdown below $200

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $48.50 resistance on volume >2M shares, or confirmation of KTOS winning defense contract tied to domestic manufacturing/reshoring initiative
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $45.00 or tariff negotiations conclude without escalation; also exit if RSI exceeds 70 without follow-through volume
tickers.risk: KTOS exposure to tariffs is indirect; primary revenue is defense contracting, not reshoring capex. Tariff reversal or trade deal announcement could collapse thesis rapidly. Also vulnerable to broader defense budget uncertainty.

events.event_title: AI Data Center Power Infrastructure Buildout Acceleration
events.event_description: Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta) have collectively committed over $300B in 2025 capex, overwhelmingly directed at AI data centers. The binding constraint has shifted to power delivery and grid interconnection. Utility-scale power equipment has multi-year backlogs. Near-term catalysts include earnings from equipment suppliers and new data center site announcements.
events.rationale: VSEC (VSE Corp) and MYRG (MYR Group) are electrical contractors directly executing data center power work with expanding backlogs. POWL (Powell Industries) makes switchgear with 18-month backlogs tied to power infrastructure. These mid-caps have direct revenue exposure without the valuation premiums of Nvidia or Eaton. Earnings revisions are a near-term catalyst.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $198.50 on volume >500k shares, or earnings beat with raised FY25 guidance on data center backlog expansion
tickers.exit_condition: RSI >70 with sell signal, or miss on data center revenue guidance; hard stop at $184 (break below support)
tickers.risk: Execution risk on project delivery delays; hyperscaler capex pivot away from power infrastructure; valuation compression if broader equity correction occurs; VSEC's diversified revenue (not pure-play data center exposure)

tickers.entry_trigger: RSI closes above 45 on volume >1M shares, or break above $215 resistance with confirmed earnings guidance raise on data center power demand
tickers.exit_condition: RSI >70 with divergence, earnings miss on data center backlog conversion, or macro reversal in hyperscaler capex guidance
tickers.risk: Backlog conversion execution risk; supply chain delays in raw materials; macro recession reducing capex; valuation multiple compression if broader market corrects before earnings inflection

tickers.entry_trigger: RSI break above 35 with volume confirmation, or close above $340 on power infrastructure contract announcement
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $320 or RSI drops back to 25; take profits at 15-18% gain or if hyperscaler capex guidance disappoints in earnings
tickers.risk: Execution risk on project delays; rising interest rates compress utility capex budgets; larger contractors (MasTec, Aecon) may capture disproportionate work; power infrastructure timelines slip beyond 10-week window

events.event_title: Defense Spending Surge — European Rearmament & US Budget
events.event_description: NATO members are racing to hit 3-5% GDP defense targets following Russia-Ukraine dynamics and US pressure. European defense budgets are at historic highs. The US defense budget remains elevated. Near-term catalysts include contract awards, earnings beats from defense primes, and ongoing European procurement announcements that benefit US exporters and specialists.
events.rationale: KTOS (Kratos Defense) builds affordable drones and target systems — direct beneficiary of both US and allied procurement. RCAT (Red Cat Holdings) is a small-cap drone maker with recent military contracts. AVAV (AeroVironment) supplies tactical drones to Ukraine and NATO allies with a clear order pipeline. DRS (Leonardo DRS) focuses on electronic systems for ground vehicles being procured heavily in Europe. ELSE (Electro Scientific Industries) — note: verify ticker — these represent the tier-2 defense electronics plays.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $48.50 on volume >2M shares with positive defense contract announcement or earnings beat; alternatively accumulate on dip to $44-45 if RSI holds >40
tickers.exit_condition: Take 50% profits at $52-53; trail stop at $47 for remainder. Exit fully on: (1) geopolitical de-escalation narrative, (2) missed contract award to competitor, (3) earnings miss on defense revenue growth, or (4) break below $44 support
tickers.risk: KTOS is sub-$2B market cap with execution risk on large contracts; exposure to defense budget delays/reprogramming; concentrated customer base (US DoD); valuation re-rating if growth slows; competitive pressure from larger primes (RTX, LMT, NOC); geopolitical sentiment reversal if Ukraine ceasefire narrative emerges

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $8.20 resistance with volume >2M shares, or pullback to $7.10-$7.30 on defense spending news confirmation
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $7.00 on volume, or take profits at $9.50-$10.50 if catalysts materialize within 8 weeks; hard stop at -8% from entry
tickers.risk: Small-cap liquidity risk, execution risk on military contracts (delays/cancellations), competitive pressure from larger primes (KTOS, AVAV), geopolitical de-escalation reducing urgency, and potential profit-taking on event hype

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $152.50 on volume >2M shares, or pullback to $145-147 support with NATO procurement announcement catalyst
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $143 (break of 200-day MA support) OR take profits at $160-165 on earnings beat + contract award confirmation
tickers.risk: Valuation compression if defense spending growth disappoints; geopolitical de-escalation narrative; competition from larger primes (RTX, LMT) capturing NATO contracts; supply chain delays reducing order fulfillment velocity

events.event_title: US Regional Bank Stress & Credit Cycle Deterioration
events.event_description: Commercial real estate (CRE) loan delinquencies are rising, particularly in office and multifamily. Several regional banks face concentrated CRE exposure as loans reprice. The Fed's higher-for-longer posture compresses net interest margins. Upcoming Q2 earnings season will be a hard catalyst with loan loss provisions and charge-off disclosures. Some banks may surprise to the downside significantly.
events.rationale: NYCB has well-documented CRE and multifamily exposure in NYC with ongoing restructuring uncertainty. CUBI (Customers Bancorp) has faced deposit volatility and has commercial loan sensitivity. OFG Bancorp has Puerto Rico concentration risk plus mainland CRE. SBCF (Seacoast Banking) expanded rapidly and faces integration and credit quality questions. These mid/small regionals have specific identifiable stress points versus the large money-center banks that are better capitalized.

tickers.entry_trigger: OFG breaks below $51.50 on volume, or earnings miss on loan loss provisions/NPA ratios; watch for negative guidance on CRE/Puerto Rico credit stress
tickers.exit_condition: Close above $54 on recovery rally, or if Q2 earnings show better-than-expected credit metrics; exit by end of week 6 if thesis invalidates
tickers.risk: Puerto Rico economic tailwinds mask mainland CRE deterioration; stronger deposit inflows could offset NIM compression; Fed pivot expectations may trigger short-covering rally before earnings

tickers.entry_trigger: Break below $76.50 on volume >2M shares OR Q2 earnings miss on loan loss provisions (>25% YoY increase) with management guidance cut
tickers.exit_condition: Close above $80.00 on earnings beat OR Fed policy pivot signals rate cuts within 60 days OR stop loss at $82.00
tickers.risk: Regional bank rally if deposit flows stabilize; CRE stress takes longer to materialize than expected; short squeeze if large positions unwind; positive surprise from loan portfolio seasoning
